title: Power Tools Basics
description: Pneumatic and electric power tools: purpose, operation and safety. 10 questions drawn at random from a pool of 15.

questions.prompt: Which tool is used together with a bucking bar to install solid rivets?
questions.explanation: The rivet gun hammers the rivet head while the bucking bar forms the shop head.

questions.prompt: What is the main advantage of a 90° angle drill?

choices.text: It drills in confined spaces a straight drill cannot reach
It drills faster in thick steel

questions.explanation: The chuck is at right angles to the motor, so it fits in tight bays.

questions.prompt: An impact wrench should be used to apply final torque to critical aircraft fasteners.
questions.explanation: Final torque must be applied with a calibrated torque wrench to the maintenance manual value.

questions.prompt: Before changing a bit on a pneumatic drill you should…
questions.explanation: Disconnecting air prevents accidental start-up.

questions.prompt: A rivet squeezer sets rivets by…
questions.explanation: The squeezer compresses the rivet between two sets, so no bucking bar is needed.

questions.prompt: Pneumatic tools should be oiled before use with air-tool oil.
questions.explanation: Oil at the inlet protects the vane motor and moving parts.

questions.prompt: Which power tool is best for heat-shrinking tubing on a wire splice?
questions.explanation: A heat gun provides controlled hot air without an open flame.

questions.prompt: A random orbital sander moves in a pattern that…
questions.explanation: The random orbit prevents directional scratches.

questions.prompt: Cordless battery tools are preferred inside an open fuel tank.
questions.explanation: Sparks from battery tools may ignite fuel vapors; use intrinsically safe equipment.

questions.prompt: What eye protection is required when using a bench grinder?

choices.text: Safety glasses or a face shield

questions.explanation: ANSI Z87.1 eye protection or a face shield is required.

questions.prompt: Which tool is used for deburring a drilled hole in a tight area?

choices.text: Die grinder with a small burr

questions.explanation: Small burrs on a die grinder reach confined spaces.

questions.prompt: The rivet set on a rivet gun should be…

choices.text: Matched to the rivet head style

questions.explanation: A mismatched set can mark the skin and give a poor head.

questions.prompt: A blind rivet tool installs rivets from one side of the work.
questions.explanation: Blind rivets expand behind the work and need no bucking bar.

questions.prompt: The speed range of a die grinder is typically…

choices.text: Very high rpm with low torque

questions.explanation: Die grinders spin 20,000+ rpm.

questions.prompt: Which of these is NOT a good practice with a pneumatic tool?

choices.text: Pointing the tool at another person

questions.explanation: Never direct an air tool at yourself or others.

title: Measuring Tools: Read the Instrument
description: Micrometers, calipers, gauges and torque wrenches — how to read and use them.

questions.prompt: One full turn of an inch micrometer thimble advances the spindle…
questions.explanation: The standard inch micrometer screw has 40 threads per inch (0.025 in/turn).

questions.prompt: The part of a micrometer that limits measuring force is the…
questions.explanation: The ratchet stop slips at a set force so readings are repeatable.

questions.prompt: A metric micrometer thimble has 50 divisions. Each division equals…
questions.explanation: One turn is 0.5 mm divided by 50 = 0.01 mm.

questions.prompt: A vernier caliper can measure outside, inside and depth dimensions.
questions.explanation: The jaws and depth rod allow all three.

questions.prompt: A feeler gauge is used to measure…
questions.explanation: Leaves of known thickness are slid into the gap.

questions.prompt: To read a click torque wrench correctly, you should stop pulling when…

choices.text: You hear and feel the click

questions.explanation: Pulling beyond the click over-torques the fastener.

questions.prompt: A click torque wrench should be stored at its highest setting.
questions.explanation: Return it to its lowest setting to relieve spring tension.

questions.prompt: What tool measures cable tension?
questions.explanation: It deflects the cable and reads tension from a dial.

questions.prompt: What is a telescoping gauge used with?

choices.text: A micrometer to measure bore diameter

questions.explanation: The gauge transfers the bore size to a micrometer.

questions.prompt: A dial indicator is mounted on a…
questions.explanation: The base holds the indicator steady against a steel surface.

questions.prompt: A micrometer should be zero-checked before use.
questions.explanation: Check zero by closing the faces cleanly.

questions.prompt: Why does a steel rule give better accuracy when viewed from directly above?
questions.explanation: Parallax causes a reading error when viewed at an angle.

title: Identify the Special Tool
description: Recognise aviation-specific tools and their parts from the 3D model.

questions.prompt: Which tool is shown in the 3D view?
questions.explanation: This is the Safety Wire Pliers (Twister). Safety wire pliers grip, twist and cut safety wire so that fasteners are mechanically locked against loosening from vibration.

questions.prompt: Which tool is shown in the 3D view?
questions.explanation: This is the Cleco Fasteners & Cleco Pliers. Cleco fasteners clamp sheet-metal layers together temporarily so holes stay aligned while rivets are installed. Cleco pliers compress the spring for installation.

questions.prompt: Which tool is shown in the 3D view?
questions.explanation: This is the Bucking Bar Set. A bucking bar is a shaped steel block held against a rivet tail while the rivet gun strikes the head. It forms the shop head by resisting the blows.

questions.prompt: Which tool is shown in the 3D view?
questions.explanation: This is the Microstop Countersink Cage. The microstop countersink cage cuts a countersink of accurate, repeatable depth so flush-head rivets sit flush with the skin.

questions.prompt: Which tool is shown in the 3D view?
questions.explanation: This is the Cable Tensiometer. A cable tensiometer measures tension in control cables, which must be within limits for the control system to work correctly.

questions.prompt: Which tool is shown in the 3D view?
questions.explanation: This is the Hole Finder. A hole finder transfers existing hole locations from a hidden or lower layer to an upper layer so that holes line up exactly.

questions.prompt: Which tool is shown in the 3D view?
questions.explanation: This is the Rivet Spacer (Fan Spacer). A rivet spacer marks evenly spaced rivet positions along a seam so spacing and edge distance meet the repair specification.

questions.prompt: Which tool is shown in the 3D view?
questions.explanation: This is the Inspection Camera / Borescope. A borescope lets a technician see inside areas that cannot be reached or viewed directly, without disassembly.

questions.prompt: What is the highlighted part of the Safety Wire Pliers (Twister)?
questions.explanation: Jaws: Grip the wire strands.

questions.prompt: What is the highlighted part of the Cable Tensiometer?
questions.explanation: Riser & anvils: Deflect the cable.

questions.prompt: What is the highlighted part of the Microstop Countersink Cage?
questions.explanation: Cutter: Cuts the countersink.

questions.prompt: What is the highlighted part of the Cleco Fasteners & Cleco Pliers?
questions.explanation: Cleco legs: Expand behind the sheet to clamp.

title: Midterm Tool Familiarization Exam
description: Timed exam: 25 questions drawn from a 30-question pool. 30 minutes, 2 attempts, 75% to pass. No feedback until you submit.

questions.prompt: What is the primary function of a bucking bar?

choices.text: Resist the rivet gun blows so the shop head forms

questions.explanation: The bucking bar backs the rivet tail.

questions.prompt: Which unit is the cleco color-code used to indicate?
questions.explanation: Clecos are sized and color-coded by hole diameter.

questions.prompt: Safety wire may be reused if it looks undamaged.
questions.explanation: Safety wire must never be reused.

questions.prompt: Safety wire twist should be approximately…
questions.explanation: Uniform tight twisting is required for a good safety wire.

questions.prompt: Which tool sets rivets by squeezing rather than hammering?
questions.explanation: The squeezer uses compression.

questions.prompt: A micrometer ratchet stop is used to…
questions.explanation: Prevents over-tightening.

questions.prompt: Which wrench is used for final tightening to a specified value?
questions.explanation: Only a calibrated torque wrench ensures correct preload.

questions.prompt: A torque wrench may be used to loosen fasteners.
questions.explanation: Loosening can damage the calibration.

questions.prompt: Pneumatic tools should be lubricated with…
questions.explanation: Air oil protects the motor.

questions.prompt: Which instrument is best for checking spark-plug gap?
questions.explanation: Feeler leaves are inserted into the gap.

questions.prompt: A hacksaw blade is installed with the teeth pointing…
questions.explanation: The saw cuts on the forward stroke.

questions.prompt: Slip-joint pliers are ideal for turning hex nuts.
questions.explanation: They round off the corners; use wrenches.

questions.prompt: Which tool prevents a drill bit from wandering at the start of a hole?
questions.explanation: The punch mark guides the bit.

questions.prompt: What should you do before changing a bit on a pneumatic drill?
questions.explanation: Always remove the power source.

questions.prompt: Which instrument transfers bore size to a micrometer?
questions.explanation: It expands to the bore walls.

questions.prompt: A cable tensiometer measures tension in control cables.
questions.explanation: It deflects the cable and reads tension on a dial.

questions.prompt: Which reference covers Hand Tools & Measuring Devices?
questions.explanation: The AMT General Handbook has a chapter on hand tools and measuring devices.

questions.prompt: A countersink cage controls…
questions.explanation: The stop foot sets the depth.

questions.prompt: Heat guns can safely be used near fuel vapors.
questions.explanation: Hot air can ignite vapors.

questions.prompt: Which unit does an in-lb torque wrench use?
questions.explanation: In-lb wrenches suit low torque values.

questions.prompt: Which tool is used to identify a hidden hole location when match-drilling?
questions.explanation: The hole finder locates holes in an underlying layer.

questions.prompt: Foreign object damage (FOD) is a major concern when tools are left in an aircraft.
questions.explanation: Always account for every tool.

questions.prompt: Which scale is read on a vernier caliper to find the last digit?

choices.text: Vernier scale line that aligns with the main scale

questions.explanation: The aligned line gives the final digit.

questions.prompt: What hardness feature distinguishes a ball-peen hammer?

choices.text: A rounded peen opposite a flat face

questions.explanation: The peen shapes metal; the flat face strikes.

questions.prompt: A mushroomed punch head should be dressed before use.
questions.explanation: Mushroomed heads can shed hazardous chips.

questions.prompt: Which PPE is required for hammering or grinding?
questions.explanation: Eye protection is mandatory.

questions.prompt: A borescope is used to…
questions.explanation: The camera probe passes through an access port.

questions.prompt: The 12 in steel rule graduations are typically in…
questions.explanation: Rule graduation depends on scale; common inch scale is 1/32 or 1/64.

questions.prompt: Which tool trims rivets to length before installation?
questions.explanation: It shears the shank to the specified length.

questions.prompt: The shop head is the rivet head formed during installation.
questions.explanation: It is formed by the bucking bar and rivet gun.
